parameters.content:
## Weekly KPI report video to Slack

Every Monday morning this workflow turns one week of KPIs (up to five
metrics) into a narrated 1920x1080 stats video — title card, one scene per
metric with a green/red delta pill (and a real sparkline whenever you
send history), then a summary grid — and drops the finished video link
into Slack. Dashboards go unopened; a forty second video gets watched.

**It runs with ZERO external data.** Leave `metricsUrl` empty and a bundled
demo dataset (a realistic SaaS week) drives the video, so your first run
needs nothing but the credentials below.

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Upload voiceover*, *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to
   editor*, *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **OpenRouter** (or any OpenAI-compatible chat API) — attach it to
   *Write narration*. Only needed while `narrate` is `true`.
3. **ElevenLabs** — add a SECOND **Header Auth** credential: name
   `xi-api-key`, value = your ElevenLabs key. Attach it to *Generate
   voiceover*. Only needed while `narrate` is `true` — set `narrate: false`
   in Config for a music-only video that needs neither LLM nor voice keys.
4. **Run it — the first run renders for real and spends about 40 credits.**
   Want a free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in Config: you get the
   exact credit quote plus an editorLink to watch the draft, nothing spent.
5. **Activate** — it reports every Monday at 9am. Point `metricsUrl` at your
   own numbers and set `slackWebhookUrl` when you are ready.

## Your metrics feed: one small JSON

`Fetch metrics` GETs `metricsUrl` and expects exactly this shape:

```
{ "period": "Jul 21–27", "company": "Acme",
  "metrics": [
    { "label": "MRR", "value": 48210, "unit": "$",
      "delta": 4.1, "lowerIsBetter": false,
      "history": [46311, 48210] }
  ] }
```

- Up to **5 metrics**, one scene each. `value` may also be a preformatted
  string ("3.2h"). `unit` is `"$"`, `"%"`, `""` or a word.
- `delta` is the percent change vs the previous period; omit it for no pill.
- **`lowerIsBetter: true` flips the colors** — churn going DOWN renders a
  green ▼ pill, spend going UP renders a red ▲.
- **`history` is optional real past values** — oldest first, ending at
  `value` (2+ numbers, last 24 kept; the key `series` also works). Supply
  it and that metric scene draws a **sparkline of exactly those numbers**,
  labelled `TREND · LAST N PERIODS`. Leave it out and the scene draws **no
  chart at all** — a centred number with its delta pill. **No trend line is
  ever invented**: nothing on screen stands in for history you did not send.
- `metricsUrl` empty → the bundled demo dataset renders (`usingDemoData:
  true` in the run summary; its numbers AND its eight-week history are
  invented sample data). Endpoint unreachable / HTTP error → demo data
  too, so a Monday report never silently skips. A 200 that does NOT match
  the contract **fails the run loudly** — you get the expected shape back.

### Wiring real sources (documented, not built in)
- **GA4** — a runReport call via a service account (or the n8n Google
  Analytics node) reduced to this JSON in a small proxy or Code node.
- **Stripe** — revenue/MRR from their reporting API, same reduction.
- Any BI tool that can serve JSON over HTTPS works as-is.

## The narration is optional

`narrate: true` (default): an LLM writes a calm analyst voice-over of the
numbers (digits spelled out so captions align word-by-word), ElevenLabs
speaks it **with timestamps**, and every scene cut lands exactly where its
sentence ends. Karaoke captions ride the real word timings.

The closing sentence the model writes is also the line printed on the
final summary card, so the last frame says exactly what the voice just
said instead of a fixed slogan.

`narrate: false`: the whole voice branch is skipped — no OpenRouter, no
ElevenLabs, no captions. Fixed scene lengths, the music bed carries the
video and the on-screen numbers do the talking. Same design either way;
with no narration the summary card falls back to `summaryLine` in Config.

On a FREE ElevenLabs plan only default voices work — Voice Library voices
return 402. Brian (the default), George, Roger, Sarah and Bill are
confirmed working.

The music bed is HEAD-checked before every render: unreachable or oversized
→ the video renders without music instead of failing.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders for real.** Set it to
`true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates the
payload, quotes the exact credit cost and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the exact video and tweak anything by hand, with nothing
spent. Nothing is posted to Slack on a dry run.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render and deliver.

## Delivery: Slack first, anything next

`slackWebhookUrl` empty (default) → the Slack step is skipped and the run
ends with the video URL in *Run summary*.

To post into a channel: create an **Incoming Webhook** in your Slack app
(api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks), paste the URL into Config. The message
carries company, period and the video link — and a `[demo data]` tag when
the bundled dataset rendered. A Slack hiccup **never kills a finished
render**: the step continues on error and the summary still has the URL.

Other delivery tails that slot in after *Run summary*:
- **Email** — an SMTP / Gmail node sending `videoUrl` to the team list.
- **YouTube (unlisted)** — HTTP Request (GET `videoUrl`, response format
  *File*) → native YouTube node, for a permanent internal archive.
- **Notion / Confluence** — append the link to your weekly review page.

They stay out of the required path so the import runs with a Zvid key and
nothing else.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button — this week's KPI report, no URL to
copy.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`) if you want to pipe the result onward.
